name: Romanian Deadlift
summary: A hip-hinge lift that loads the hamstrings and glutes through a long range while the lower back works to hold a neutral spine. Useful for posterior-chain strength and hamstring size.
setup: Stand holding the bar at hip height with an overhand grip just outside your thighs, taken from a rack or lifted from the floor.
Set your feet about hip width apart with a soft bend in the knees.
Pull your shoulders back and down, brace your trunk and keep your arms straight.
execution: Push your hips straight back while keeping the bar close to your legs.
Let the bar slide down your thighs with a flat back and a soft, fixed knee bend.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, usually around mid-shin, before your back begins to round.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall.
Keep the bar in contact with your legs the whole way.
cues: Squeeze the glutes at the top
mistakes: Rounding the lower back: stop the descent earlier and brace harder before each rep.
Bending the knees too much so it turns into a squat: keep a fixed soft knee angle and send the hips back.
Bar drifting away from the legs: keep your lats tight and drag the bar along your thighs.
Leaning back at the top: finish by standing tall with the glutes, not by hyperextending the lower back.
